If you like a good soundtrack, character customization, art style and narration then you’ll be loving every second Bastion has to offer. Bastion is an hack and slash action RPG that combines an amazing art style with an even more amazing soundtrack.
The combat and movement feels smooth and unique. There is a variety of different weapons that allows you to fight enemies the way you want. One of the best things about Bastion is the freshness of the game, there aren't many games that are able to pull of an amazing art style, soundtrack, narration and combat all at the same time. The scenery never gets boring and is alway changing with lots of minor details. One of the ways they do this is by having the ground around you form as you walk near it. This can help keep people with low attention spans to keep engaged with the game.
The constant improvements to your character and weapons gives a lot more replayability to the game. Leveling up allows you to quipt a buffing effect called a ‘spirit’ to your character. Weapons can be upgraded through finding materials when exploring the world. Idols make the game harder in certain aspects and are used to give the player more of a challenge, this helps give the game more replayability. The hack and slash gameplay is well made with lots of different ways to defeat your enemies. Upgrading weapons was very satisfying and fun to do. Bastion's soundtrack is very good and interesting and can be what keeps some people playing the game. The art style is also very unique and fitting with the soundtrack.
One of the cons the game has (And it’s hard to come across cons in Bastion) is that the hack and slash gameplay at times can get a little repetitive. It’s also lacking in a filled in story, for example It doesn’t talk about what the world was like before the calamity, leaving the world feeling a bit empty at times. The story missions are basic and revolve around collecting one sort of object for almost every mission. But these don’t make Bastion a bad game, far from it. These are just little things I found when playing Bastion other people might and probably do disagree with.
On average Bastion takes around six and a half hours to complete the story, while to complete the story and all extras takes around twenty hours. Bastion keeps the story nice and short for players looking for a short and sweet experience, while giving the game a good amount of completion hours for those wanting to spend a good extra fifteen or so hours on the game. With this and everything I’ve covered I’d recommend this game to anyone who loves good hack and slash mechanics, art and soundtrack in the games they play. I think It’s well worth the full price of fifteen dollars, but if you find it on sale it’s a must buy.

For now, hold off on your purchase - there are many, many things which need implementation or fixing, even for an early access game it's a little surprising. The reason I'm giving a negative review, despite hoping the game gets better down the road, is simple - I cannot recommend it in its current state. No, it's not just because it has bugs - it's in early access, of course it's going to have bugs. However, I do expect early access games to have some standard of quality. I think they need to be at least somewhat playable - the core of the game being somewhat functional with missing features or placeholder assets / audio, along with a lot of minor bugs, a few major bugs and poor optimisation to be ironed out is fine by me for early access. Some documentation on how one should play the game in order to test it effectively is welcome (but not needed).
In this game's current early access state however, it is nowhere close to that - the core game is completely unplayable for more than 12 minutes. A line needs to be drawn on what's acceptable and what is not for general release to the public, both for the consumer's and developer's sake, as the reputation an early access game gets can also have an effect on its reputation during release. The developer should have known this and not caved into the fan's demands (people have been demanding for the past year for the devs to release something, no matter what state it is in, which is wrong) - it will give them a quick buck in the short term, but it may have dire ramifications long term, which is a shame.
If you wish to support the developers or assist their efforts in bug fixing (like I have - I really want The Guild 3 to be a good game hence my purchase and time spent so far despite its unplayability), then by all means get it now. For those who actually want to play it, I cannot recommend it - steer clear from this until the next build.

As one of the few people who discovered Transistor before this, it's difficult to view Bastion without comparing it to its Supergiant sibling. While there are plenty of similarities, from Darren Korb's western-infused soundtrack to the charming gravel-voiced narrator, Bastion feels brasher and a little more immediate. The art style is lovely and vivid, the story is fed to you in an informal fashion that allows you to absorb or reject as much as you feel like and the combat, in comparison to Transistor, is much more immediate, giving you enough customisation to allow you to match to your own playing style but relying more on reflexes than on strategy. Also, the addition of Idols is a novel twist on the difficulty setting format and can allow for some serious challenge as the game goes on. In short, great story, incredibly fun and well worth a punt.

Kingdom Rush is by far my favorite tower defense game - it has diverse maps, very cute graphics, fun creatures, it's simple to get the hang of, but also has challenges for those who want them. I've played the browser version from start to end multiple times and it's great that it's available on Steam as well, with achievements, trading cards and all.
There are 26 levels in total and 3 game modes (campaign, heroic and iron challenge), along with 3 difficulty levels (casual, normal, veteran). You have 3 base types of towers and can choose between 2 specializations for each upon upgrading them. Stars you earn for completing levels are used for additional upgrades of your towers and abilities/spells. There are also heroes that can be moved around the field where they are most needed. The gameplay is dynamic and offers enough flexibility without making it hard to manage the towers and the movable units at the same time. The upgrade system is simple and you can max everything if you get enough starts. While some people find the game repetitive, I was never bored and loved every bit of it!
My only complaint is that Ironhide don't intend to port the other Kingdom Rush games for Steam and I have to play them on mobile (which is not my primary choice of gaming platform...). There probably won't be any more updates to the Steam version, so with that in mind I think the price is a bit steep; you might want to wait for a discount. Other than that, it's a great game and if you're a fan of the TD genre (or a newbie who's looking for a nice start), I recommend you Kingdom Rush.

I beat the game and was really pleased, only to find out that I still had half the game left to complete, sort of...
I hate frustration platformers, but the first half of this game nailed the right level of difficulty for me. It mixes a rhythm game with a platformer, where as it goes on you'll need to use the abstract but enjoyable electronic music in order to time your movements.
Visually it's extremely simple, but surprisingly appealing and even beautiful at times. Screenshots absolutely do not do it justice. I feel the slick animations in time with the music and sound effects, particularly in the boss encounters, raise the visuals above what you'd expect from such simple assets. Even the way the character morphs between shapes while jump and move is brilliant, even better than the squash and stretch animations of Thomas Was Alone.
Mechanically I felt the game did an excellent job at throwing new ideas at the player constantly, while giving concise organic lessons before throwing them into something more difficult. Each of the 3 bosses I fought had that small learning period as well. The checkpoints are frequent and I was rarely frustrated. It seems some players aren't even aware of the "second half", as they only appear if you go through the main menu back into the game, and go just further to the right than you had to go the first time. These 3 extra levels seem to be identical to the original 3, but mirrored left to right, using different color combinations, with permadeath... I didn't realize it the first time I tried the first mirrored level, until I died and spawned back at the intro. I decided to give it another crack and I was able to complete it without dying on the next try. The level of stress shoots through the roof, as the whole level becomes as tense as the hardest sections of the game. I don't really enjoy that level of difficulty, specifically the concept of punishing failure with repetition, but in this case it's not really extra content, so it can be safely skipped if you're not up to it.
My playtime so far, beating 4 of the 6 levels was just shy of an hour, but I quickly fell in love with it's simplicity. It doesn't match the charm of Thomas Was Alone, or the unbelievable visuals of FEZ, but it's damn good for what it is. It runs flawlessly at 120FPS at 1080P, but it probably supports higher resolutions as well. I played with a keyboard rather than a controller because I honestly just started it to see it, but it hooked me and I ended up beating the whole thing in one go. Pricing is up to the buyer, but I'd say it's certainly worth the asking price on a moderate sale, or in one of the dozen bundles it's been in.

Our mercenaries were ambushed by werewolves. They outnumbered us easily 2 to 1. After they swarmed the spearmen, the archer was charged and killed. We were well equipped with good armor and helmets.
The melee started out well, no damage taken and some given, but the arms of men grew tired and heavy. We were unable to keep up the shield wall, and sometimes unable to even to do any more than defend the torrent of claws. 4 men became three, three became two. Some beasts were felled, some fled, but they were still to many. In time, one man stood before 4 werewolves.
He was unscathed, but he was exhausted. He was scared, but he could not flee. He was surrounded. So he fought. He killed one, but his armor and helmet were shredded beyond usefulness. He stabbed at the wavering wolves, as if he could fill them with fear by filling them with the cold steel tip of his spear. He killed one as it turned to flee, killed another that got the same idea. More -- one, two, he couldn't know -- howled from the nearby darkness. And one stood before him, flailing at him with its claws, the claws found flesh, and he bled, but he continued to fight.
In the end, Emmerich stood alone, buried his friends, and walked alone to the nearest town with bloody spears, claw-torn shields, and seven large black wolf pelts.

This game is still in the early stages but despite some issues it has the potential of being a very good game. The game play is rather straight forward and the company development is interesting and make you want to keep them alive to see how they develop. Things are still rather linear for now and can be frustrating when in combat on your newer recruit has only 14% chance to hit and always seems to connect while you veteran gets 80% a misses every time he attempt to hit anyone.
Another major frustration is that the enemies seem to die very hard when totally surrounded. You would think that the advantage of attacking an opponent on all sides would make it a full gone conclusion but far to often that is not the case. I have lost members of my company more often than not when the last enemy is surrounded and should be crushed. However ,it is early days and one hopes that those events become less likely.
One last current annoyance is the lack of feedback as to what is happening. Why do zombies resurrect time and time again and how does one stops this? I mean how often do you have to kill the same opponent? Also the damage received and dealt is not very clear. The current side interface that does explain some of what is going on is not very clear and makes the events happening rather guess work. A number value on hit points, armour points would be better than a small simpler bar showing the current state of affairs.
Despite the complaints it is a fun game. The idea of adding magic, factions, town and city development would make it even better. I would recommend giving the game a chance as it is rather old school but in a very good way and I sure the money provided by your purchase will help the game develop into a potential gem. So in conclusion the game is still a little rough but I think with the right feedback and additions this will turn out to be a polished little gem of a game.

Bought this game the other day and way more addictive than I would have thought.  Solid turn-based combat with nice RPG elements.  Reminds me of a game I used to play as a kid - Fantasy General - in some ways.  There's way more technical critiques on here that are good but the game definitely gets my vote.  For an early release it's polished enough to be a lot of fun for 20 hours or so.
Some suggestions for future upgrades:
Day/Night Cycle and Marching - The game has great resource usage, days passing, and interesting/impactful vignettes - most taking place 'in camp at night.'  I'd recommend having movement more turn based with your company marching during the day and camped at night.  Makes the vignettes more realistic and could add a whole new dimension to the game.  Setting your march time/speed could impact the readiness/fatigue of your troops.  You could have options for setting defenses/watches at night, etc.  It could make caravan escorts more fun as well to march alongside the caravan with a turn - but be ready for attacks at night.  Enemy structures could have 'zones' of operation - meaning the danger of raids on your camp or caravan increase.
Size of the Company - 12 is great for shield-wall and RPG intimacy.  But, doesn't feel like you're really building a powerful mercenary force.  As you progress it would be great if you could 'promote' a member to a team/squad/platoon/company leader.  Then you could recruit more mercenaries into that formation - but the icons could stay the same, maybe with some mini-portraits at the base of the character icon on the battle map.  It would allow you to keep increasing the size of your force to be more and more powerful.  The same would go for your enemies.  Would be a way to increase the difficulty and scope of all the different types of enemies.
Support Personnel, non-combat - I love the use of food, maintenance, ammo, and paying the troops.  It would be awesome if your company could have a hireable/modifiable support staff you could manipulate as the mercenary band commander.  A blacksmith/armorer to maintain/upgrade your equipment, a paymaster to keep the troops paid/fed, a medic to heal the troops - you might even consider a spy/scout leader to affect the fidelity/distance of information about the enemy.  Opens a whole new area for effectively managing your mercenary band.
Flag and Shield Design.  Using the symbols provided let the player design their own flag, then paint their shields with the logo as well.
Reputation - I've seen this suggested other places and think it's a great idea.  It would be awesome to have your actions impact your reputation with factions - could effect pay, enemy encounters, available jobs, cost of items, etc.
Prisoners/surrender - You could have a certain portion of enemies (or your own) not die outright and be available as prisoners at the end of a battle.  You could ransom them back, recruit them to your company, get extra pay for bringing someone back alive, etc.
A couple of things I don't care for as much:
The elevation mechanics seem like they still need to be worked out.  Mine don't show up well in the graphic interface and advantages/disadvantages aren't as apparent.
Fatigue, it's a good concept but really penalizes heavy troops.  It would be nice if there was a way to get troops able to wear heavy armor without having to level them up so many times.
Levels should keep going past 11,
Would like to be able to compare equipment effects a little easier - and more varieties of equipment.
Would be nice to have some control over how battles start when you initiate - aren't ambushed.
Battles can go on quite some time trying to chase down fleeing or retreating foes.
No way to toggle a character inactive when you're in the final stages of a battle and trying to finish off the last couple foes - but are limited with how many troops can attack.
All-in-all it's a great game with a ton of possibilities.  I really hope you keep improving it and it pays off financially for the developers.

Stranded Deep is a game that I want to check out and play because it looks pretty, and you survive against nature, and the inevitable online coop it will have, which will be hopefully awesome.
You will probably say this looks like 'The Forest' , whether you say it's better or worse, I'm going to say both look and play very similar, but both walk a different path in terms of the setting, and the way you survive in it.
So let's talk about the good stuff. It's definitely a good looking, one of the best lookers out there. It plays good with simple controls, nice fluid UI, and a nice new form to craft where you drop your items on the ground, and then you will have a menu show up that will give you option on what you can craft depending on what you're holding in your hand, and what you have on the ground, and that's kind of neat.
Crafting items is easy, and so is collecting them is, by picking up rocks, sticks, leafs..etc. About build a shelter, it's sort of like the game called 'Unturned' where you have to make a foundation, supporters, walls, and then a roof. You can put stairs too if you want.
The sailing from one island to another is neat, it's functional, but still needs a lot of work and hopefully more variation in terms of what you can ride on, like build an actual boat or something. This area could definitely use improvements, comparing it to another game called 'Salt' which I consider an expert in terms of sailing and exploration.
Diving, hunting crabs and fish with your spear, and if you want go ahead and attack a shark. Speaking of sharks, they're not as threatening as I thought them out to be, you sail from one island to another, if you keep going they don't attack, if you stand still on your boat you still don't get attacked, if you go and take a swim they don't attack unless they're behind you only, and do little damage as far as my experience went, heck I attacked them and tried to hunt them down, they ran away which was funny.
The game is fun, it needs a lot of work, but simple yet complicated, natural survival games are fun, especially if they look good, intuitive, and sail. Going back to a comparison between Stranded Deep and The Forest, aside from their different direction they're going for, The Forest has more work put into it in terms of immersion with it's animations, graphics, and it has more charm and life, and if Stranded Deep wants to push on immersion, it should definitely look at The Forest, and in terms of fun, intuitive sailing experience, and island generation variety, they should take a look at Salt. Heavily.

Okay... so I'm completely re-writing this review because the 1.0 came out, and I finally played the game all the way through. And my final thoughts?
Ehhhhh...
TL;DR VERSION: Yeah, I still love it.  Great exploration and building game with a few minor issues.
Okay, first off, TO THE LIST!
Positive:
+Vast universe to explore
+Visually pleasing
+Great soundtrack
+More action-oriented than Minecraft, but less so than Terraria - an interesting niche, since it’s neither completely Zen like the former or completely hectic like the latter. Nice!
+Easy to use construction tools
+Lots of different items and architecture to uncover/craft
Neutral
+\- The story's only meh. It's not bad, it's just not all that great, either
+\- A lot of the weapons/items are not worth much by the time you get them
+\- Very, very tiered exploration (you can go to this kind of planet... okay, now you can go to these..)
+\- The "magic items" (Wands and Staffs) are functional and fun, but feel completely out of place in an otherwise science-fiction game
Negative
-Despite the RNG, limited range of possibilities makes all the planets more or less the same
-The NPCs in the game more or less fall completely flat
-There are only three side quest - kill a guy, find a guy, gather some stuff so I can impress a guy. Doing them feels tedious after a very short time
-Although this is true of most similar games, the NPCs that populate your colonies are completely useless
-This might just be me, but there's almost no difference between playing the different races, and that bugs me
Let me get the negatives out of the way first. The worlds you visit become repetitive fairly quickly, and that makes me sad. There just isn't enough variation, which might be because of the limited block/geography types, or it might be the RNG itself, but despite having literally thousands of different planets to choose from, they all more or less feel the same. This means that after a certain point, you may find yourself moving only between three places - the Outpost (a kind of "hub" for the main quest line), wherever your permanent colony is, and wherever the current story-quest has you running off to. In other words, the exploration part becomes boring and repetitive, which makes me very sad since it's what I was hoping for most from this game.
Unfortunately, the biggest letdown is the NPCs. You can get crew members for your ship, but they’re mostly only good at dying (they provide small buffs, but nothing you really need) and they’re not very interesting to talk to. They can also be a pain to recruit, since you have to do multiple fetch or other quests to convince them to join you - and you only find out if they would be willing to join you after you complete those quests. At each major “boss” stage after the first, however, you do meet some fun, competent, and well done NPCs… but you can’t have them on your crew. Disappointing.
The Side Quests, which can be picked up from a large number of NPCs in the game and function similar to Radiant Quests in Skyrim, are just repetitive and boring. They all follow one of three variations:
1.Go find my friend and lead them back here
2.Go kill this guy/these guys
3.Go talk to a bunch of people for me/gather a bunch of stuff for me so I can impress someone else - repeat like three times
It’s not especially fun, which is bad enough, but you have to do these side-quest shenanigans in order to gain crew members… which, as it turns out, isn’t worth the effort as I’ve already said. Colonists at any colonies you build are, if anything, worse - they offer up the same quests, but also get angry with you if you make the wrong changes in the colony you built in the first place. They also don’t… really do anything. It is my sincere hope that, one day, a game like this will appear where the “colonists” (or what have you) build things themselves while you’re out doing other things. It would add soooo much verisimilitude. Instead, I wind up being the nanny for a bunch of adults.
And then there’s the Race Selection. I like all of the races available for PCs to choose from, and the available customization is incredible. There’s a pretty vast lore behind the races, too, and when investigating individual items, they all say different things, in the voice of their particular race. I’m especially fond of the Floran (fun savagery), the Glitch (Statement: Glitch have an interesting method of emotional expression), and the Hylotyl… And there’s a big issue right there, off the bat.
There is no mechanical difference between the races - none. While reading the occasional interesting comment is kinda neat, and having customization options is grand, there really should be some kind of mechanical difference. For instance, Glitch could be immune to radiation but sink like a rock in the water, Floran could regain energy faster in sunlight but slower in the dark, Hylotyl could breathe under water and swim a bit faster but move slower on land, Avians could have a glide ability but have less HP - anything. Anything like that, even if it was only a very minor difference, would have been wonderful. Instead, I played through the whole single player campaign as a fish person who couldn’t breathe under water on their own, even though the Hylotyl lore states they were chased beneath the waves…
All of the above aside, though, it’s still a pretty great game from a pretty great developer. The music is great and does exactly what incidental music should do in a game - reflect the current “mood”. It’s visually very pleasing. Everything works together to make controlling your character a joy. Combat is fun, construction is easy, and crafting feels satisfying (most of the time).
I still recommend this game - it's worth the low asking price for sure, and there are mods that can add some extra variation to the game and fix some of the issues I described above. Even without the mods, it's a great game. The developers (Chucklefish) are also one of the best indie distributors out there, and they deserve the support. You don't have to feel bad about liking/buying this game: Chucklefish are genuinely good Devs/Publishers with hearts of gold... or maybe something from a higher tier, I dunno.

I really like horror games but I don't like the feel of the DS, so a PC port of this game seemed like a great idea. I put it on my wishlist and it went on sale a week later so I purchased it. Originally being a DS game I wasn't expecting much out of the graphics, nor do I really care about graphics, and I think they are just fine. Animations are very jumpy and really could have been smoothed out for this HD version, though. I did find the atmosphere and creature design to be quite impressive. In regards to design, I would put some of these monsters among the best in the horror genre. The story is also fine but it's not a huge focus and doesn't get in the way too much, except when it gears you towards little fetch quests. After that, it mostly falls apart. Ammo is pretty rare to find, weapons have major recoil and it feels like every enemy is a bullet sponge. The melee combat is pretty rough as well, making the combat a chore and since that is the bulk of the game play, that's a very bad thing. With the exception of boss fights most of the enemy AI is designed to run/fly straight at you, so there's not much strategy or planning you can do with the combat either. You just take your melee weapon and smack each other until you or the enemy die. Then you load up on health pills and move on. The sound effects aren't too bad but the background music primarily consists of a very short violin loop during combat that many people will likely find annoying. The one thing I did like about that music is that it is a good indication of when an enemy is nearby that you might not have seen. Adding to the problems this game is fairly buggy and I found a few instances where buttons/keys didn't work and I had to restart the game to resolve.
Overall I can't recommend this game. Major mechanics need a complete overhaul and though it might be fine for the DS, it does not comparatively hold up against other atmospheric first-person games on PC like Doom 3 or Condemned.

I would also point out that even by 2013, the graphics aren't amazing, but it is an indie title, so I don't mind giving wiggle room.  The sounds were all great and were used well to create an uneasy atmosphere.  There is a constant droning sound that will get under your skin, and it's supposed to.  Most of the enemies were pretty well thought out, but a few were pretty throw away.  If I had once major complaint it's that dang revolver.  It's terrible.  I claim no responsibility for it never hitting anything...
Anyway, it's a bit under rated, and it's probably not for everyone.  I don't think it's a masterpiece and there are plenty of games I would recommend before this, but if you have played everything you had planned to in the near future and have some free time, I'd say pick this up. A breathtaking exploration of the possible synthesis between platforming level design and rhythmic games.
This is a wonderfully immersive experience, meaning that the senses of touch (controls) hearing (rhythmical patterns) and seeing (the graphical representation of what's going on in the music) are synthesized into one concentrated state in which you can't differ one from the other.
It's  a game with a steady difficulty curve and great ideas which are communicated from the developer to you, using  only the simplest of controls, graphical means and music to pose greater and greater challenges.
The game is quite short, but I did not beat the final boss, because it is really hard. I know how to beat him, but the challenge is its randomness and concentrating on many distracting and counter intuitive things going on at once, which is quite brutal.
I imagine the synthesis between game and player to be at its height when the player is concentrated enough to fight this final boss.
I would recommend this game to anyone who likes rhythm games or is interested in what computer games can be when genre boundaries are not taken too seriously. I can also wholeheartedly recommend it too people who are into music visualization and abstract art/electronic music because this game has ideas in spades for all of those.

Bought this game the other day and way more addictive than I would have thought.  Solid turn-based combat with nice RPG elements.  Reminds me of a game I used to play as a kid - Fantasy General - in some ways.  There's way more technical critiques on here that are good but the game definitely gets my vote.  For an early release it's polished enough to be a lot of fun for 20 hours or so.
Some suggestions for future upgrades:
Day/Night Cycle and Marching - The game has great resource usage, days passing, and interesting/impactful vignettes - most taking place 'in camp at night.'  I'd recommend having movement more turn based with your company marching during the day and camped at night.  Makes the vignettes more realistic and could add a whole new dimension to the game.  Setting your march time/speed could impact the readiness/fatigue of your troops.  You could have options for setting defenses/watches at night, etc.  It could make caravan escorts more fun as well to march alongside the caravan with a turn - but be ready for attacks at night.  Enemy structures could have 'zones' of operation - meaning the danger of raids on your camp or caravan increase.
Size of the Company - 12 is great for shield-wall and RPG intimacy.  But, doesn't feel like you're really building a powerful mercenary force.  As you progress it would be great if you could 'promote' a member to a team/squad/platoon/company leader.  Then you could recruit more mercenaries into that formation - but the icons could stay the same, maybe with some mini-portraits at the base of the character icon on the battle map.  It would allow you to keep increasing the size of your force to be more and more powerful.  The same would go for your enemies.  Would be a way to increase the difficulty and scope of all the different types of enemies.
Support Personnel, non-combat - I love the use of food, maintenance, ammo, and paying the troops.  It would be awesome if your company could have a hireable/modifiable support staff you could manipulate as the mercenary band commander.  A blacksmith/armorer to maintain/upgrade your equipment, a paymaster to keep the troops paid/fed, a medic to heal the troops - you might even consider a spy/scout leader to affect the fidelity/distance of information about the enemy.  Opens a whole new area for effectively managing your mercenary band.
Flag and Shield Design.  Using the symbols provided let the player design their own flag, then paint their shields with the logo as well.
Reputation - I've seen this suggested other places and think it's a great idea.  It would be awesome to have your actions impact your reputation with factions - could effect pay, enemy encounters, available jobs, cost of items, etc.
Prisoners/surrender - You could have a certain portion of enemies (or your own) not die outright and be available as prisoners at the end of a battle.  You could ransom them back, recruit them to your company, get extra pay for bringing someone back alive, etc.
A couple of things I don't care for as much:
The elevation mechanics seem like they still need to be worked out.  Mine don't show up well in the graphic interface and advantages/disadvantages aren't as apparent.
Fatigue, it's a good concept but really penalizes heavy troops.  It would be nice if there was a way to get troops able to wear heavy armor without having to level them up so many times.
Levels should keep going past 11,
Would like to be able to compare equipment effects a little easier - and more varieties of equipment.
Would be nice to have some control over how battles start when you initiate - aren't ambushed.
Battles can go on quite some time trying to chase down fleeing or retreating foes.
No way to toggle a character inactive when you're in the final stages of a battle and trying to finish off the last couple foes - but are limited with how many troops can attack.
All-in-all it's a great game with a ton of possibilities.  I really hope you keep improving it and it pays off financially for the developers.

Let's review Fallout 4
I enjoyed the Fallout franchise, and i cannot understand why the hate behind Fallout 4 but in my opinion:
Pros - Its a good story, not the best i reckon but it still had a feel to it.
- Plenty of side missions to wander around a big map and discover all you want.
- Plenty of easter eggs if you know how to search for them ;)
- Lovely old timey soundtrack, that excels in providing the correct set of mind required to play this game
- Although not a complete fan on the introduction on base building in this franchise, after playing with it a bit i wanted to better my base and actually care for my people, so they won me over with that.
-Successful in the creation of a faceless villain, which you can ( depending on your choices) be a part of it.
- Sub stories that add alot to the Lore of Fallout
- Tough decisions and easy ones.
- Extensive weapon modification and XP gathering for those different levels and perks.
Cons : - Some ocasional graphic bugs but nothing game breaking as is now. (15/12/2017)
- DLC are a bit expensive so wait for deals.
- There isnt a "level" of added dificulty for that extra challenge, i found the game quite easy.
- Some of the Side Quests are just Rinse and repeat, with little to few alterations, luckly they are just a couple but still.
- Dont venture into the Creations aspect of the game, it blows and is just a money grabbing operation for stupid stuff.

Final Review - This game is good, i give it a 7.5 out of 10, but it has the potential to be one of the great games out there, here's to hoping the next one can learn on these mistakes and improve to give the avid fan of the Fallout Franchise what they truly deserve worthy of the name.

I'm a fan of Turn Based squad games, started with FF Tactics on an imported Psone, played many since then Tactics Orge, Disgea, Silent Storm, AOW, Valkyria etc my favorite (at the moment) being the new XCOM. But Battle Brothers could trump them all, Hopefully the Devs will continue as they've started, Im sensing a real inteligence and understandng of what makes a good turn based strategy game. The basics are really REALLY GOOD battling is solid and tactical, I've battled alot in this game as its the most fleshed out aspect, like taking your starving beaten squad making your last stand on a hill for the height advantage, having 40 Bandits surround you, managing to kill one of the strongest bandits with a crossbow and watching as the rest of the bandits start waivering and eventually after some luck and judgement coming out the winner, its very satisfing if not fairly unlikely, You could play the same battle and have completely different outcomes depending on what you choose to do, its GREAT. Also being able to equip your soldiers with bows at the beginning of a battle and then switching to shield and spear as the enemy advance and combining different abilities and perks together is a very nice touch so much scope for tinkering, I've come across very little in the way of bugs or problems, I had so many battles with one particular character that it be nice to know how many kills hes had, as hes probally had almost a hundred hopefully stats will be added in future updates, he will mostly likely be wiped before that happens (EA of course) wiped but not forgotten.
I can almost feel the love and care in this game, your little guys level up you can re-name them choose what they wear which then shows on the character, theres a unique way of recruiting soldiers reading their back story which then has a bearing on their stats, good stuff. I wasnt sure on the graphics at first but after diving in I fell in love with the art style simple yet detailed and very consistent, All round top marks.  Its bare bones Early Access stuff at the mo but i'm confident that if these devs continue with the same passion they have started with then this will be one of the best turnbased strategy games around. All I want is more of everything characters, story, missons, castle towns hideouts, your own base, equipment etc just more of everything please.  I strongly recommend you support this game if you like RPG Turn-Based Squad fun and games.

First Impressions (Will update with more experience later)
Visually this game is breathtaking, Being that you're around water so often I can't help but abosolutely love the look of it, when you look into it from your raft you can see quite deep which feels very realistic when you're swimming total blackness is common and  a very scary feeling. The sense of exploration and adventure in this title is amazing, I often found myself needing a little courage before jumping in the water out of fear of tiger sharks or any of the other predators that lie about. Attention to detail is quite nice to, I killed a crab with my knife and then ate it to which I took damage (I'm assuming either by the shell or because it's raw) I love that this game doesn't hold you hand, it throws you on an island and you have to survive with expirementation. It gives you just enough helpful supplies to make your stay not impossible but not enough to make it easy. Even with only a couple hours of gameplay I can honestly say this game has much potential, I'm not saying it's good yet, that takes more time. But I am enjoying it.
EDIT
Crafting: Ok I tested out some of the crafting aspects now and I can say at the start I absolutely hated the whole drop mechanism for crafting. Basically you bundle everything on the ground and then use items and tools to craft different things from the ground. After a while I really took a liking to it however, I'm not sure why but it feels realistic. If I was on a island I can't help but believe I would start gathering and sort my materials on the ground until I decided what I should do with them, although this isn't huge I really enjoyed this method of crafting. I also like that a foundation can be either a floor or a raft, let's face it, they're not much different just a bunch of sticks tied together, really great idea making both into one craftable item. Overall I really like the Crafting system.
Fishing: I only fished for a short while but visually it's great, the fish stick to your spear and wiggle around a bit, feels very realistic (not that I go around stabbing fish).
EDIT
Sharks: Shark AI seems very decent. I decided to go out and try to fight one off and it was a very close fight, the movement is what I immediately noticed, they move like a natural predator where they will sneak in for a bite then go into the depths and come back in for another attack. They're also extremely weary of confrontation so if you start swining a knife at it it will swim away. Very nice could definitely be a bit more difficult though.
Bugs: Currently theres a very annoying bug that will make you lose your raft in the middle of the ocean, this happened to me twice in a row where I had no choice but to swim to the island.
Again will update with more info when I see it necessary.

Okay... so I'm completely re-writing this review because the 1.0 came out, and I finally played the game all the way through. And my final thoughts?
Ehhhhh...
TL;DR VERSION: Yeah, I still love it.  Great exploration and building game with a few minor issues.
Okay, first off, TO THE LIST!
Positive:
+Vast universe to explore
+Visually pleasing
+Great soundtrack
+More action-oriented than Minecraft, but less so than Terraria - an interesting niche, since it’s neither completely Zen like the former or completely hectic like the latter. Nice!
+Easy to use construction tools
+Lots of different items and architecture to uncover/craft
Neutral
+\- The story's only meh. It's not bad, it's just not all that great, either
+\- A lot of the weapons/items are not worth much by the time you get them
+\- Very, very tiered exploration (you can go to this kind of planet... okay, now you can go to these..)
+\- The "magic items" (Wands and Staffs) are functional and fun, but feel completely out of place in an otherwise science-fiction game
Negative
-Despite the RNG, limited range of possibilities makes all the planets more or less the same
-The NPCs in the game more or less fall completely flat
-There are only three side quest - kill a guy, find a guy, gather some stuff so I can impress a guy. Doing them feels tedious after a very short time
-Although this is true of most similar games, the NPCs that populate your colonies are completely useless
-This might just be me, but there's almost no difference between playing the different races, and that bugs me
Let me get the negatives out of the way first. The worlds you visit become repetitive fairly quickly, and that makes me sad. There just isn't enough variation, which might be because of the limited block/geography types, or it might be the RNG itself, but despite having literally thousands of different planets to choose from, they all more or less feel the same. This means that after a certain point, you may find yourself moving only between three places - the Outpost (a kind of "hub" for the main quest line), wherever your permanent colony is, and wherever the current story-quest has you running off to. In other words, the exploration part becomes boring and repetitive, which makes me very sad since it's what I was hoping for most from this game.
Unfortunately, the biggest letdown is the NPCs. You can get crew members for your ship, but they’re mostly only good at dying (they provide small buffs, but nothing you really need) and they’re not very interesting to talk to. They can also be a pain to recruit, since you have to do multiple fetch or other quests to convince them to join you - and you only find out if they would be willing to join you after you complete those quests. At each major “boss” stage after the first, however, you do meet some fun, competent, and well done NPCs… but you can’t have them on your crew. Disappointing.
The Side Quests, which can be picked up from a large number of NPCs in the game and function similar to Radiant Quests in Skyrim, are just repetitive and boring. They all follow one of three variations:
1.Go find my friend and lead them back here
2.Go kill this guy/these guys
3.Go talk to a bunch of people for me/gather a bunch of stuff for me so I can impress someone else - repeat like three times
It’s not especially fun, which is bad enough, but you have to do these side-quest shenanigans in order to gain crew members… which, as it turns out, isn’t worth the effort as I’ve already said. Colonists at any colonies you build are, if anything, worse - they offer up the same quests, but also get angry with you if you make the wrong changes in the colony you built in the first place. They also don’t… really do anything. It is my sincere hope that, one day, a game like this will appear where the “colonists” (or what have you) build things themselves while you’re out doing other things. It would add soooo much verisimilitude. Instead, I wind up being the nanny for a bunch of adults.
And then there’s the Race Selection. I like all of the races available for PCs to choose from, and the available customization is incredible. There’s a pretty vast lore behind the races, too, and when investigating individual items, they all say different things, in the voice of their particular race. I’m especially fond of the Floran (fun savagery), the Glitch (Statement: Glitch have an interesting method of emotional expression), and the Hylotyl… And there’s a big issue right there, off the bat.
There is no mechanical difference between the races - none. While reading the occasional interesting comment is kinda neat, and having customization options is grand, there really should be some kind of mechanical difference. For instance, Glitch could be immune to radiation but sink like a rock in the water, Floran could regain energy faster in sunlight but slower in the dark, Hylotyl could breathe under water and swim a bit faster but move slower on land, Avians could have a glide ability but have less HP - anything. Anything like that, even if it was only a very minor difference, would have been wonderful. Instead, I played through the whole single player campaign as a fish person who couldn’t breathe under water on their own, even though the Hylotyl lore states they were chased beneath the waves…
All of the above aside, though, it’s still a pretty great game from a pretty great developer. The music is great and does exactly what incidental music should do in a game - reflect the current “mood”. It’s visually very pleasing. Everything works together to make controlling your character a joy. Combat is fun, construction is easy, and crafting feels satisfying (most of the time).
I still recommend this game - it's worth the low asking price for sure, and there are mods that can add some extra variation to the game and fix some of the issues I described above. Even without the mods, it's a great game. The developers (Chucklefish) are also one of the best indie distributors out there, and they deserve the support. You don't have to feel bad about liking/buying this game: Chucklefish are genuinely good Devs/Publishers with hearts of gold... or maybe something from a higher tier, I dunno.

Το Northgard είναι ένα παιχνίδι που ανήκει στα είδη Indie, Simulation, Strategy αλλά και αυτή τη στιγμή βρίσκεται σε Early Access μορφή. Είναι ένα αριστούργημα της Shiro Games της οποίας οι ιδρυτές είναι ο Nicolas Cannasse και ο Σεμπάστιεν Βιντάλ. Υπάρχουν πολλά παιχνίδια με θέμα τους Vikings όμως ας δούμε τι έχει το Northgard που το κάνει μοναδικό.
Η εταιρεία έχει δημιουργήσει άλλους τίτλους παιχνιδιών όπως το Evoland και τον διάδοχο του το Evoland 2 και φυσικά το Until Dark.
Story
Το παιχνίδι είναι βασισμένο στους Vikings γνωστούς από την Σκανδιναβική μυθολογία. Αρχικά υπάρχουν 5 διαθέσιμες φυλές στο παιχνίδι αυτή τη στιγμή, ενώ στο κοντινό μέλλον θα κάνει την προσέλευσή της μια νέα φυλή. Ξεκινάμε από την πρώτη φυλή που ονομάζεται Fenrir και έχουν ως έμβλημα τον λύκο. Είναι μια επιθετική φυλή η οποία υπερασπίζεται την ελευθερία της κάθε φορά. Η επιλογή της Fenrir είναι αρκετά καλή γιατί όλες οι μονάδες σας καταναλώνουν λιγότερο φαγητό κατά 30% και προσφέρουν Hapiness. Το Hapiness βοηθά στην δημιουργία περισσότερων μελών της φυλής. Σειρά έχει η Eikthyrnir με σύμβολο ένα άγριο ελάφι. Η συγκεκριμένη φυλή προσφέρει φαγητό, ξύλο αλλά και χρήματα στην αρχή, πράγμα που σημαίνει ότι η Eikthyrnir παίρνει μεγάλο προβάδισμα στα πρώτα στάδια.
Η επόμενη φυλή είναι η Heidrun η οποία έχει ως σύμβολο την κατσίκα και συγκεκριμένα το αγριοκάτσικο. Η Heidrun εξασφαλίζει άφθονο φαγητό γιατί ξεκινάτε με 2 πρόβατα και μπορείτε να τα σκοτώσετε και φυσικά να λάβετε κρέας. Καλό θα ήταν να χτίσετε ένα Sheepfold για να έχει μεγαλύτερη παραγωγή. Αξίζει να σημειωθεί ότι κάθε φορά που διοργανώνετε ένα feast, λαμβάνετε 30% περισσότερη παραγωγή σε όλους τους τομείς. Περνάμε στην επόμενη φυλή,την Huggin and Muninn με σύμβολο το μαύρο γεράκι. Είναι εξερευνητές και φυσικά καλοί διαπραγματευτές, θα κάνουν τα πάντα για να συνεχίσουν να ταξιδεύουν και να εξερευνούν νέα πράγματα. Γι’αυτό στην αρχή έχετε την ευκαιρία να χτίσετε λιμάνι για να ανακαλύψετε νέες περιοχές. Τελευταία και καλύτερη κατά την γνώμη μου πάντα είναι η φυλή των αρκούδων ή αλλιώς Bjarki. Στην αρχή μένει αρκετά πίσω διότι δεν λαμβάνει κάποιο σημαντικό bonus ενώ κατά την περίοδο χειμώνα που συχνά δυσκολεύει τους περισσότερους παίκτες είναι σε καλή θέση γιατί η μείωση του φαγητού και του ξύλου μειώνεται κατά 30%. Επίσης όλες οι στρατιωτικές μονάδες σας λαμβάνουν 10% προστασία κατά τη διάρκεια του χειμώνα. Αξίζει να σημειώσουμε ότι μπορείτε να εκπαιδεύσετε μια αρκούδια στο training camp σας. Η αρκούδα ή η «Kaija, The Armored Bear» όπως ονομάζεται στο παιχνίδι είναι πολύ δυνατή στης μάχες. Αυτές οι 5 φυλές μάχονται για το ποια θα κυριαρχήσει.

Gameplay
Ξεκινάτε απλά με το town hall το οποίο «παράγει» νέους κάτοικους. Αμέσως ξεκινάτε να χτίζετε καινούργια κτήρια όπως σπίτια (Houses) για να έχετε την δυνατότητα να φιλοξενείτε περισσότερα άτομα στην πόλη σας. Μια καλή επιλογή είναι να χτίσετε Scout camp ώστε να ανακαλύψετε πολλά μέρη στο χάρτη γρήγορα και να πάρετε προβάδισμα. Για να κερδίσετε την παρτίδα θα πρέπει να τερματίσετε πρώτος σε μια από τις τέσσερις (4) κατηγορίες. Αρχικά η «Domination«, που έχει ως μοναδικό στόχο την νίκη ενάντια σε 3 διαφορετικές clan. Σειρά έχει η κατηγορία «Fame» η οποία απαιτεί αρκετά περισσότερα πράγματα από την πρώτη. Πρέπει να ελέγχετε 12 περιοχές στον χάρτη, πρέπει να έχετε 1200 gold που δύσκολα κερδίζονται και τέλος πρέπει να έχετε χτίσει το «The Altar of Kings».
Η 3η κατηγορία ονομάζεται «Trade» και έχει 3 στόχους. Ουσιαστικά είναι καθαρά εμπόριο. Πρέπει να έχετε στην άκρη 1000 νομίσματα ή αλλιώς krowns, να έχετε μαζέψει συνολικά 9000 krowns (gold) μέσω του εμπορίου και να έχετε 4 merchants/sailors ενεργούς. Ο τελευταίος στόχος είναι αρκετά εύκολος. Τελευταία και καλύτερη κατηγορία για εμένα, η κατηγορία «Wisdom» η οποία σχετίζεται με τις ανακαλύψεις σε μνημεία και έχει 2 στόχους. Τέσσερις loremasters/sailors πρέπει να είναι ενεργοί αλλά και πρέπει να έχετε 4 «blessings from the gods». Κατά την γνώμη μου η πιο εύκολη κατηγορία είναι η «Wisdom».
Technical
Τα γραφικά του τίτλου είναι πολύ ωραία και απλά. Υπάρχουν πολλές λεπτομέρειες στους χαρακτήρες όσο και στο φυσικό τοπίο. Πιστεύω, ότι η επιλογή για τα απλά γραφικά ήταν σωστή γιατί τα περισσότερα παιχνίδια αυτού του style έχουν βαριά graphics υψηλής ευκρίνειας που τελικά καταλήγουν περισσότερο αποσπαστικά παρά βοηθητικά. Το γεγονός ότι έχει απλά γραφικά το κάνει ξεχωριστό σε σχέση με τα άλλα. Όσο αναφορά τον ήχο, η μουσική είναι πολύ όμορφη, και φυσικά μέσα στο κλίμα. Σου δίνει την ιδέα ότι είσαι και εσύ ένας από τους Vikings. Η μουσική αλλάζει ανάλογα με τις εποχές, και βέβαια την κατάσταση gameplay (σε μάχη, κάνοντας εμπόριο κτλπ). Αξίζει να σημειώσουμε ότι οι φωνές των ανθρώπων και οι «κραυγές» είναι κάπως αστείες. Δεν ξέρω για εσάς αλλά εγώ γέλασα παραπάνω απ’όσο έπρεπε, αν και να πω την αλήθεια μου άρεσε. Τέλος τα ηχητικά εφέ, όπως όταν για παράδειγμα οι ξυλοκόποι κόβουν δέντρα, είναι αρκετά ρεαλιστικά.
Final Verdict
Έχοντας περάσει πάνω 10 ώρες με το παιχνίδι, έχω σχηματίσει την τελική μου γνώμη. Αρχικά, πιστεύω ότι σε γενικές γραμμές είναι πολύ ωραίος τίτλος αλλά κατά την γνώμη μου και με βάση τα ελληνικά δεδομένα, η τιμή των 20 ευρώ είναι αρκετά υψηλή. Αν βρείτε το παιχνίδι σε έκπτωση από την άλλη είναι διαφορετική ιστορία. Το συνιστώ σε όσους είναι λάτρεις των Strategy παιχνιδιών και σε όσους τώρα θέλουν να ξεκινήσουν την πορεία τους στον κόσμο των παιχνιδιών στρατηγικής.
Στην πλήρη τιμή του είναι ένα χλιαρό thumbs down, αλλά αν το πετύχετε σε προσφορά δοκιμάστε το, θα το αγαπήσετε!

This isn't quite the game I expected. From the images posted I was really expecting a vikings style Banished but with a talent tree and more combat. What the game actually turns out to be is Settlers, but without meaningfull traderoutes.
The game isn't bad at all though. While still in it's early access the game tends to feel a bit hollow.
PROS:
- The graphics are fun and lighthearted
- Setting villagers to work many differant jobs!
- My inital reaction to the game is that it is very multiplayer focused.  Randomly generated maps and tile spawns keep the game fresh every time.
CONS: This list is quite larger..
- Tiles. The tile system doesn't feel good at all. Combat is really held back due to the system not allowing you to enter into enemy lands without taking each tile before it. Resource hoarding to buy additions tiles feels akward as well.
Each tile has a set amount of buildings you can build on which feel extremely restricting. You want that Fishing node, Iron node and deer? Go right ahead, but now you cant build a food silo or that house you needed without saving up again to purchase another tile.
- Resources. I think the resource gathering system needs some improvement. There is little feedback if you are trying to collect fame or lore. You set your villagers to harvest lore or fame and then wait. The rewards being a couple more talent points or one time fame bonuses. Not much thought goes into those victory conditions.

- Combat. Probably the weakest part of the game. Units can be micro'd when they enter into a tile but when you try to move between tiles it can get very buggy. There is only a handfull of soldier units and each clan shares the same units except for a commander unit in most cases. Healing in the game requires villagers to have that job, which is fine. But the time it takes to heal units vastly slows the game down making late game pushes a pain.
- Balance. The wolf clan will beat everyone. They focus mostly on early game attacking which can easliy steam roll a player within 15 minutes or less. All it takes is for you to guess correctly where the enemy is and then you can all in your villagers into combat units and neglect your economy.  Your enemy HAS to immidiatly plan for your invasion as soon as the game begins and they always have to plan around whatever you decide.
Like I said, it's early access but the game is good. Once the game has a campaign and is more fleshed out it's going to be great even. I'm not the biggest fan of the tile and building system, but with more added into those systems I feel it can become very rewarding. I'd also like to see a lot more differances between clans.
Only saying "No" to recommendation because there isn't a "Mixed" button. If you enjoy Settlers, get the game now!

This game takes a little bit of everything: your classic base building, a bit of Settlers and some Civ XYZ. The game's premise is to build a settlement and basically meet one of several types of victory conditions, including but not limited to: domination, trade, research and map event(s).
Your domain is controlled by borders which you can expand with Krones (currency) or food, the latter of which increases per amount of controlled territories, so it's not a case of just expanding your base willy nilly - which also means you're limited to structures per territory, meaning you have to strategically think about where you're going to place each structure (towers are NOT affected by this limitation.)
And to cover quickly the last topic: Your military is also limited by your Warband capacity, meaning you can focus on your military by just constantly building Warband Camps (increases +2, or +3 upgraded) and create a relatively big army. The most units I've personally ever had is x1 Bezerker, x3 Warriors, x3 Axemen and x2 Shield Bearers.
• Fun, aesthetically pleasing graphics.
• Excellent intuitive gameplay.
• Nordic/Fantasy themed.
• Balance is extremely satisfying (especially with the Bear clan).
• Villagers actually have an idle role meaning they gather food when not doing anything (so useful.)
• Winter is hard and challenging, so are the dynamic events like rats, earthquakes, etc.
• Some mechanics don't make sense and some aren't implemented (i.e. Forge).
• Villager spawn rate can sometimes be infuriating.

If you're a fan of tower defense games, and haven't playd Kingdom Rush, you're seriously missing out. The game is tough as nails, but it's so rewarding once you get it down.

The mobile app received more love from the developers, and has two extra DLC sets -- Frontiers and Origins. They load the game up with a few new tower upgrades, interesting new levels, new enemies, and new heroes. The desktop version of this game, for some reason, never got these updates and is vastly behind in the amount of content. It's unlikely that they'll add it. The biggest benefit to the desktop version of this game is that you don't need to pay for heroes, whereas the mobile apps have a pretty strong paywall on some of the heroes they offer.
That being said, I still enjoy the desktop version of this game very much. It's nice to play it with a mouse and a large screen, which makes your reaction times faster and doesn't have you hunched over your phone/tablet.

If I could give this game an 8/10, I would, but Steam doesn't work like that.  The game currently has 97% positive reviews which seems overrated, so I'm downvoting it.
Bastion has fluid gameplay, adaptable weapons, and adjustable difficulty with the shrine that gives enemies additional abilities if you find them too easy.  It also has new game+ and score attack if you want to push things to the limit.  The narration is innovative as well since it talks in real time while you progress through levels, but you can turn its volume down if you don't like it.
However, the game isn't all that.  If you're 10-13, and this is your first time playing a game with a sophisticated plot, you'll like it.  If you've played or read sophisticated plots in the past though, the game will seem bland.  It really isn't that sophisticated, and even though there are flexible level select options as well as proving grounds to earn extra weapon abilities and upgrade, it's still pretty linear.  At the end, you have two dilemmas to decide upon, but they really don't make a difference.  You don't get to playthrough an aftermath, and the only consequence is different dialogue from the narrator and some different ending credit pictures.
This game had the potential to be truly epic a la Chronotrigger/Chronocross, but as soon as you decide on those dilemmas, the game's over.  You're left asking for more, and feel like you just read through chapter 3 in a 10 chapter book where the author forgot to write the rest of it.   The game dumps you into the middle of things, and while it gives a little backstory, you never get to make decisions in playing through it.
In a sense, the game feels like Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning in that it trades plot for action.  The action is good, but not excellent.  Many of the weapons are just copycats of each other with little nuances that let you trade them off.  The enemy attack patterns are standard and predictable as well even though the difficulty is gradually ramped up.
Ultimately, Bastion is a solid purchase, but nothing more.

The main problem is the absolute lack of polish. There's so many issues that I couldn't possibly remember them all, but the basic gist is that the game is annoying to play. You can't pause the game. Whenever you switch weapons there's multiple seconds of delay. Your inventory is forced into five different tabs you can't look at the same time. Trying to find the right item when you want it is always a small chore. The multiplayer is completely unoptimized. Balance is bad, especially early on. Achievements, a driving force for a lot of players, are completely hidden in the Steam interface and don't include descriptions. Several of those achievements are needlessly grindy for no reason. Wildlife on planets are a nuisance and discourage exploration. There's NO way to mitigate falling damage. Food doesn't stock. Food rots over time. When it rots you have to move it one piece at a time to a different tab to get it to stack. Food rotting, hunger, and lack of teleporting when there's a roof over your head REALLY discourages exploration. For some reason the final tier of the anvil is made by adding one of three addons which give you different items to create. You can't have all the addons in at the same time to see what's available at once so you have to tediously replace them each time. You can't do much with the grapple hook because everything useful like mining or using the matter manipulator uses two hands, so you better get used to CONSTANTLY be making platforms.
The main storyline is a lather/rinse/repeat every tier.
Grind out new ores -> Build new armor/weapons and upgrade breathing device -> Do the "Scanning" quest for whatever Species the Tier is centered on -> Do the Dungeon for whatever Species the tier is centered on. -> Repeat for every tier.
There are some neat things here. Building and colony management isn't bad. But there's just too much in here that seems designed to be unfun and annoying for me to recommend this to anyone.
If you ignore this warning and decide to play anyway, I recommend playing on "Casual" mode. It removes a lot of annoyances like the Hunger mechanic (which continues to deplete during unskippable cutscenes. Players die during those), reduces currency loss on death, and allows you to beam back to your ship from anywhere.
If you like crafting survivals and haven't played Terraria before, just go play that with a friend instead.

Third time I've reviewed this game now, I wouldn't normally bother but a lot of the complaints I made are now outdated so... lets do this again xD
Battle brothers is not for everyone, I'll be honest about that, it hasn't got the prettiest graphics and it requires a bit of thought in your decisions. That being said if you can get past the initial difficulty curve (and it's not a massively hard one) this becomes one hell of a rewarding game to play. This is a game where your characters, with all their hard-earned skill, can be killed at a moments notice if you're not careful. It's a game where you can lose hours of painstaking progress levelling up a character simply because you forgot to give him a helmet. But ♥♥♥♥ me if it isn't rewarding.
Taking a brawler from one of the starting locations and forging him into a steel-clad badass with a greatsword is one hell of a feeling. Marching into the center of an orc warband and in your head screaming "come get me". All the time aware that one misstep can send your character down permanently. And I do mean permanently - permadeath is a key mechanic of this game and you will not be able to avoid it.
Whilst the game, in my opinion, is absolutely fantastic, it still has one things I would like to see in updates or perhaps a sequel if it sells enough to warrant one: whilst I understand the low-fantasy setting and thus the lack of having magic available I would love for that to become a mechanic in the game. Aside from that I honestly think this game is a beautiful combination of XCOM, Final Fantasy and Lord Of The Rings.

Dementium II was a generally loved game on Nintendo DS, however things turned for the worse when we've got a high definition edition. At its core, Dementium is not scary at all, not fun to play, outstays its fledgling welcome, sounds and looks positively abominable and leaves terrible first impression.
One of the rare pluses in this game is somewhat interesting level design that is quite reminiscent of old Resident Evil games as you are traversing a puzzle layout of rooms. There's a well implemented metroidvania style of backtracking as new levels are unlocked as you pick up certain weapons and items, that were previously inaccessible. Also game works from start to end without any major bugs ruining what's left to enjoy in this game.
Minuses aplenty: graphics look worse than the original Half-Life from 1998, which is especially damning since Dementium II was released almost ten years later, and the HD edition 15 years from Half-Life. Artistic direction is also equally as poor, as you are traversing yet another asylum with bland look and feel. Music is completely unimpressive and barely worth noticing, while sound mixing is all over the place as some enemies scream so irritatingly loud that you'll get ear bleeds if you are using microphones, while firearms and dynamites sound extremely muted and poor. Shooting and walking is very imprecise and floaty, which I suppose is what developers wanted to do to put you in the shoes of a common poor sod that sounds like he's blasting a dookie every time he tries to jump. Story and dialogue is full of clichés we've seen for a thousand time now, and told in such an appallingly bad manner that saying a kid wrote this would be an insult for all the kids out there.
Dementium II HD is a poorly design, implemented and written game that does nothing to evolve horror genre for a single iota. If you want a quick and cheesy horror game romp, you can find on Steam better games than Dementium II on every corner, and if you want to play a horror classic, then just forget about Dementium II alltogether.

To date with so many new 3D + hero TD games, is Sanctum 2 still relevant? Very much so I'd say.
Sanctum 2 is the next installment of Sanctum. The aliens are back and it's your duty to once again defend the core against these pesky aliens. Sanctum is a 3D Tower Defense game with a Hero concept & that allows First Person Shooter. Sounds complicated? Back then, yes it was. Now days, it seems like a norm concept.
You play as 1 of the "hero" characters and  your job is to protect the core from the alien invasion. They come in all sizes but mostly in blue color..with 1 and 1 only goal in their mind: SMASH. YOUR. CORE.
That 2 sentence practically sums up you entire sanctum 2 gaming experience. Laugh or Cry, its a fact in all co-op game. Sanctum 2 is a brilliant product that melds hero + fps + tower defense in 1 game play. On top of that, you are also given comic strips as a story and some rewarding in-game cut scenes for the completion of certain maps. The end product is one satisfying game play experience. While no wacky element is present like Borderlands 2 or Trine,  (I am pretty sure there are some that wished Sanctum 2 could be a little light heart-ed..or 1,2 screw loose somewhere =p ) It still delivers the intended co-op game play experience. I guess you'd need some jokers to be in your game to lighten up the mood. Too many serious people around you and you'll feel like you've just enlisted into the army defending a blue ball.
Controls are fairly easy to master. The tricky part is knowing the primary & secondary abilities.
I'd also wished there was an easier way to identify which towers were at what levels.
Visually, its goods. You'll probably notice that every "good" game has their own visual art. Sanctum 2 has a great visual art. It's strange..and yet interesting. Walking Blue bloops. Mini swarm of C4s. A Giant Glowing Bulp with 2 legs?! Undead astronauts ?!
Audio wise, I dont have much complain nor compliment. Nothing soothing apart from the "timer countdown" sound and the constant yelling of team mates "QUCIK! BUILD IT! FASTER! OMG!" I'd probably say the devs could have put in 2 more sound tracks instead of the calming ambient background music throughout the entire battle. Some of us want some "noisy" songs you know.. xD
My Personnel Experience:
70% of my gaming experience has been describe in the 2 sentence above. The other 30% experience is my own solo play. When it comes down to tactics, it seems like theres a simple rule to do it. Cheap. High Rate of fire. Decent Damage. and 1 support tower. That's practically it when you play solo - however when you play with others, that logic does not apply anymore because you now have 4 player & assuming each takes a different tower you are going to have 16 different towers. The issue then is, do you play quality or quantity TD ? I always set up 2 choke points with quality towers. Orbital is my name baby! It's slow, its expensive but it gets the job done - the way i like it. A hole in the ground. filled with dead blue aliens. many many dead blue aliens. not just 1. but MANY. *evil laugh*
5 feat strength game mode is the ultimate challenge. You'll need a team to achieve it else ..solo can only get you up to a certain point of the game/map. More than that you'll go insane repeating the same map with various towers excepting to survive the blue wave.
The Campaign
The story of the campaign was decent. I bought Sanctum 2 with the DLC's so on my last mission I had to witness 2 lovers parting..while it certainly makes the fight more meaningful or memorable, I am just wondering when did those 2 become lovers in the first place? Was it forced into the story? Kinda felt awkward..but more reason for me to come back into Sanctum 3 to reunite these lovers. again. If we are presented with the choice of doing so that is.
My Summary
Sanctum 2 puts you through long hours of battle with the aliens (and humans. Most of the time its the darn humans.) The journey will put you into a roller coaster ride of emotions: fun yet torturing, annoying but grateful..lastly a strong sense of satisfaction you can find no other game has...when you smash your teammate into oblivion with your tower *evil laugh*
So, on the scale of 0 - 10, my personal rating for Sanctum 2 is an awful orbital strike of 8/10.

Sure, I listed more negatives than positives but you'll definitely be getting your money's worth from the hours you'll likely spend playing it. Wickland is an indie arena shooter heavily inspired by classic FPS games of the 90's. Morph into eight deadly beasts and use their own unique abilities, blaze through maps at insane speed to pick up power-ups, and fight your friends or foes in classic maze-like arena maps, just like the good old days. Wickland is an arena FPS dedicated to PC Gamers.
Set in what seems like Midievel times, Wickland brings back that oldschool fps feel that we all remember from the early 2000's. There are 2 modes at the moment including what they call "Warm up" which is basically just FFA Deathmatch and Duel Mode which is a basic 1v1. Both are fun to play but I find FFA a lot more fast paced and fun. Weapons are very similar to those of Quake and even imitate them in a midievil way. Instead of keeping the same character through the game though, you switch between them on the go by simply scrolling or pressing a number key, each character having a different weapon. Health pickups, Ammo, Armor and Weapons spawn around the map and must be walked over to be collected all respawning a short time later.

This review was intended for the definitive edition, I somehow posted it here by mistake, still, it will be  just as relevant here:
I loved the original release of this game. Sure, i did have my share of performance issues when it first came out (mainly, major microstutter), but a few updates later and I was suddenly playing all of my favorite Hong kong Cop movies, these neatly packaged into one exceedingly awesome and well crafted game. Sleeping Dogs accomplishes exactly what it sets out to achieve, all of which is remarkably well executed, and built with close attention to detail. At heart this adventure is a faithful hommage to one particularly under appreciated genre of cinema.
To put this simply the gameplay just works, even if opting for the mouse and keyboard, which I did. Everything is fast, tight, fluid ,enguaging and overall, has surprisingly lew bugs to detract you from the experience.
There's a fair amount of meat to bite into here. If you start out intending  to complete all that it has to offer, Sleeping Dogs will keep you busy for just over 40 hours, (add another 10 - 15 hours to that if you're achievement hunting.)
As for the story, it does, at times, fall into the genre's tropes and cliches, and while that might of proved a reproach in another context, were i might of been reviewing a different game, here, despite the events often seeming predicatble and familiar (That is, If you're as much into to these eastern police Dramas as I am) it comes accross feeling fully intended to be as such, as though this familiarity was precisely what the writers had envisionned from the very start. The result is a faithful, fun  and memorable amalgamation of all the elements that make for a great hong kong police drama.
At the end of the run, when it was all said and done and I saw those ending credits scroll down my monitor, I had my hat off to it, smiling like an impressionable idiot while I sat there, fully content with my experience. Shortly after, in days that followed, I proceeded to binge watch every Chow Yun-Fat flick I managed to get my hands on.
On a closing note, when I first heard about there being a definitive edition with upgraded graphic on the way, I didn't really see any point to it, I mean to me, the original release was by no measure an ugly looking game, quite the contrary, it looked darn amazing, I thought. That said, this new release does succeed  in raising the bar it set for itself with the first release, proving that it fully mertis its title: The definitve edition.

Witckland is a Quake style shooter where you pick up weapons that change you into to strange mideval (?) fantasy monsters that have different magic powers that work like traditional guns. There is a werwolf, ape man, and many more creatures. I like the concept of a weapon changing your whole character, and would like to know if other shooters use this premise.
The levels are all dark castles, so setting can be a bit dull, but the levels are well designed.
This game uses a health and armor system where you can pick up power ups to heal like traditional 90s shooters. The controls are very tight and great.
The main issue is all forms of servers are dead. Meaning the only form of gameplay is bots. Bots are super mobile and accurate, so they can provide a great challenge if you are into that sort of thing. Also you can use external programs to make a server with your friends temporarily and play. But I don't have friends with the interest to put in the effort, and assume others would be in the same boat.
Achievements are a small factor in games, but can add a fun moment or extra challenge. Achievgements here are just win a large amount of games. Which is impossible without hours of planning and grinding. There are no unique, funny, or furfilling skill based achievements.
I got this game out of a bundle with a bunch of game I did want, and if servers were still working/ easily accessible it would have been a treat. The bottom line is there are dozens of shooters that have working servers to get similiar gameplay (although maybe without such a fun and unique theme.)
I rate the game 6/10. It's nothing spectacular, but it's serviceable in fun. But being dead, comparatively difficult when compared to other games to get a single game going; I can't reccomend it. If someone knows a shooter with a similiar theme, aesthetic, or mechanic where you're whole character changes based on the weapon I'd love to try it out.

So first impressions are not very good, the game is lagy and only gets 25fps. The graphics are not the best, and the UI does not fully work. In the options menu the sliders did not work.
I think that if you are wanting to buy the game to play, wait for the game to develope more, but if you want to support the development of the game and help with bug fixing then go ahead and buy it.
In my personal opinion I think that the more people who buy it the better the game will turn out because the devs then have more eyes and ears helping discover bugs, and just giving them feedback on the game.
So again if you want to support the development of the game then go ahead and buy it, but I would recommend that you wait till the full game is released or until the game has been developed more.
Besides there still is another option that you can choose to do, which is play "The Guild 2: Renaissance", which is one of my favorite games on steam, dispite not having many hours in the game.

If you are a newcomer to the series, the last paragraph is for you!

Should definitely mention that it is Early Access and as the devs said, there are bugs and placeholders so if you're looking to buy into this Early Access be aware of that. I think, aside from being a fan of the previous titles, buying into this EA is mostly to give feedback to the devs as testers. The game is going to be sold at a lower price during EA and raised to full price once the game is released ($50/$60USD?)
Graphics are a upgrade from Guild 2, however, the priest class is missing from the game. Will update if devs are going to add or not. The character voices are.. Not good, lol, sound a bit like robots reading a script. Game's UI is rough.  MP is currently not playable, devs are still working on it should be ready for release hopefully. In the current build, theres still a lot missing from Guild 2, looking at the
, hopefully this fleshes the game out, I really hope they add more interactions with buildings, doing things inside it, etc. GolemLabs needs to add more to this game gameplay-wise even more things not listed in the roadmap before I consider it better than Guild 2.
This game is essentially manage your dynasty as you try to gather wealth and power in Medieval Europe. You start a business (farming, manufacturing, etc) and eventually try to run for a political office. The game right now in Early Access state is a bit rough to play and if you don't know what you're doing you will probably be confused. My guess is, if you have money to spare or know youre going to buy this game, go ahead and grab it while it's discounted before full release. If you're on the fence I'd suggest just waiting til full release and to get a full taste of the game rather than it in it's current EA state.
Overall, how they go about this early access will really decide if they make or break the game, are they going to go Divinity 2 route and do Early Access right or fumble along and ruin the series? As of right now, game is too risky for a buy and but give it a few months in early access. I'd say mostly for fans of The Guild series it's a cautious buy. If you're new to the series I'd definitely say sit and wait on updates. I feel most of the negative reviews are people not really understanding what Early Access entails or even bothered to read what the dev had to say about the early access build so I wouldn't put much stock into these reviews.
